arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident originating from external IP 185.220.101.42 led to a pass-the-hash attack affecting all 23 user accounts in the Finance OU. Initial access was achieved via exploitation of a low-criticality IT asset (WS-IT-101, 10.0.2.15), which was previously scanned from the same external IP. The compromise went undetected at the point of lateral movement and privilege escalation. Attempts to revoke credentials via IAM/PAM were denied due to lack of approval and insufficient evidence linkage in the system.

Detection of anomalous authentication patterns from host 10.0.10.51 triggering UEBA and SIEM investigation.
Analysis confirms pass-the-hash attack affecting all 23 accounts in Finance OU. Bulk credential revocation attempted.
IAM/PAM actions denied due to policy restrictions and insufficient automated evidence correlation.

The external IP 185.220.101.42 conducted reconnaissance via port scanning against an internal IT asset (WS-IT-101 at 10.0.2.15), which was later used as a pivot point to access the Finance OU. Critical finding issued: 23 Finance OU accounts compromised via pass-the-hash. Bulk credential revocation attempted.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was initiated via a phishing email that delivered a malicious payload through an encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook. The payload executed a reflective DLL injection via rundll32.exe from the user's Temp directory, establishing a C2 beacon over HTTPS to a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23). The attacker performed reconnaissance and lateral movement across 200 production servers. Containment actions to disable critical service accounts and rotate credentials were denied due to lack of pre-approval, highlighting a gap in incident response authorization protocols.

rundll32.exe loaded unsigned DLL from Temp directory (T1218.011), establishing C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
